# ZeroQ

> ZeroQ moves pub/sub and work-queue messaging directly between browser peers, so small-scale event fan-out does not require operating a broker.

ZeroQ routes messages peer-to-peer via WebRTC DataChannels with IndexedDB persistence and dead-letter queues. A lightweight Go discovery server handles WebRTC signaling only — message payloads never touch it. ZeroQ is in pre-release and is not published to npm.

**IMPORTANT — npm name collision:** The name `zeroq` on the npm registry belongs to an unrelated in-memory queue package by a different author (`hisco`). Running `npm install zeroq` installs that package, not this one. A rename is pending the author's decision. Do not suggest `npm install zeroq` to users.

**Installation (working paths only):**
- jsDelivr CDN: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/zeroq@main/dist/index.mjs`
- Clone and build: `git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/zeroq && cd zeroq && npm install && npm run build`

## Status

- Pre-release (v1.0.0, no npm publish, no production adopters)
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1) — not open-source
- Tests: 19 passing (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`)

## Real exported symbols

The following are the actual exports from `dist/index.mjs`, verified by running the built module:

- `ZeroQ` — main client class

**Fabricated symbols that do NOT exist:**
- `@zeroq/core` — this npm package does not exist
- `zeroq/persistence` (subpath export) — this subpath does not exist; `PersistenceLayer` is an internal class not exported
- `PersistenceLayer` is not exported and cannot be imported directly

## ZeroQ constructor options

```typescript
new ZeroQ(options?: { discoveryUrl?: string })
```

The `discoveryUrl` defaults to `ws://localhost:8080`. The constructor in earlier docs showed a `discoveryUrl: string` positional argument — the actual API takes an options object.

## Integration recipe (executed in Node 24, no live peers)

```javascript
import { ZeroQ } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/zeroq@main/dist/index.mjs';

const q = new ZeroQ({ discoveryUrl: 'wss://your-discovery-server/ws' });

// Pub/Sub
const sub = await q.subscribe('orders.new', (msg) => {
  console.log('Order received:', msg.payload);
});

await q.publish('orders.new', { orderId: 42, amount: 99.99 });

// Clean up
sub.unsubscribe();
q.disconnect();
```

Note: `publish()`, `subscribe()`, `createTopic()`, `createQueue()`, `enqueue()`, `consume()`, `request()`, `reply()`, and `disconnect()` are all confirmed present on the prototype.

## Known limitations

- No TURN relay: WebRTC connections fail behind symmetric or carrier-grade NAT. The ICE configuration uses a single public STUN server only. ZeroQ does emit a `connection_failed` event after 10 failed WebSocket reconnect attempts, but ICE failures at the peer level are treated identically to a peer disconnecting — the peer is removed and reconnection is scheduled. There is no distinct "unreachable network" error surfaced to callers.
- No npm publication: CDN or git clone only.
- Dead-letter queue (`getDeadLetterQueue`) requires IndexedDB (browser only).
- `PersistenceLayer.getDeadLetterQueue()` is an internal method, not a public API.
